questions.q: Four students record the same kind of wire. Dev writes 147/100 m, Esha writes 1 4/10 7/100 m, Farah writes 1 47/100 m and Gita writes 14 7/10 m. How many of the four records show the same length?
questions.a: Three: Dev, Esha and Farah

questions.q: A pencil is 5 3/10 5/100 cm long (5 units, 3 tenths and 5 hundredths). (a) Write its length in hundredths only. (b) A second pencil measures 548/100 cm. Which is longer and by how many hundredths?
questions.a: (a) 5 units = 500 hundredths, 3 tenths = 30 hundredths, so 535/100. (b) 548 hundredths is more than 535 hundredths, so the second pencil is longer by 13 hundredths.
s: Part (b): compares 548 with 535 and states the gap of 13 hundredths

questions.q: Two lace pieces measure 2 6/10 m and 1 7/10 m. They are joined end to end and then 1 9/10 m is cut away from the joined length. The lace left is ___ tenths of a metre.
Create a real-life situation in which a length of 53/10 units is measured. Then write that length as a mixed form.
questions.a: Any sensible story, e.g. a tailor measures a strip of lace as 53 one-tenths of a metre. Mixed form: 53/10 = 50/10 + 3/10 = 5 3/10 m.
s: Gives a realistic measuring situation that uses 53/10

questions.q: A ribbon is 3 4/10 m long. (a) How many pieces of length 1/100 m can be cut from it? (b) How many pieces of length 1/10 m can be cut from it, and how does the count in (a) compare with this one?
questions.a: (a) 3 4/10 m = 34/10 = 340/100, so 340 pieces. (b) 34 pieces of 1/10 m. The count in (a) is 10 times as large, because each tenth holds 10 hundredths (340 = 34 x 10).
s: Part (b): 34 pieces of one tenth, and 340 = 34 x 10 since each tenth holds 10 hundredths

questions.q: A craft teacher cuts strips of length 3/10 m, 3/100 m, 33/100 m and 30/100 m. (a) Write all four strips in hundredths. (b) Arrange them from shortest to longest. (c) Two of the strips are equal. Name them and explain why they are equal.
questions.a: (a) 30/100, 3/100, 33/100, 30/100. (b) 3/100 < 3/10 = 30/100 < 33/100. (c) The 3/10 m strip and the 30/100 m strip are equal: each tenth is 10 hundredths, so 3 tenths = 30 hundredths.
s: Part (a): converts 3/10 to 30/100 and keeps the others in hundredths

questions.q: A helper writes a length as '6 12/10' and says this is a mixed form with fewer than 10 tenths. Show that this is impossible and rewrite the length correctly.
questions.a: 12/10 is 12 tenths, which is more than 10 tenths, so it makes 1 whole unit and 2 tenths. A mixed form with fewer than 10 tenths cannot hold 12 tenths. 6 12/10 = 6 + 1 + 2/10 = 7 2/10.
s: Notes 12 tenths is more than 10 tenths (more than 1 unit)
Explains the extra unit must move to the whole part

questions.q: A school rope-climb rope was knotted from three pieces of lengths 2 7/10 m, 3 6/10 m and 1 9/10 m. (a) Write each piece in tenths only. (b) Add them in tenths. (c) Write the total as a mixed form. (d) A new rope is 80/10 m long. Which rope is longer and by how many tenths?
questions.a: (a) 27/10, 36/10, 19/10. (b) 27+36+19 = 82 tenths. (c) 82/10 = 8 2/10 m. (d) 80/10 = 8 m = 80 tenths; the knotted rope has 82 tenths, so it is longer by 2 tenths.
s: Part (a): converts the three pieces to 27, 36 and 19 tenths
Part (d): compares 82 with 80 tenths and says the knotted rope is longer by 2 tenths

questions.q: A tape measures 29/10 m. (a) Write the length as a mixed number and say how many full metres it holds. (b) Strips of 4/10 m are cut from it. How many full strips can be cut and what length is left over?
questions.a: (a) 29/10 = 20/10 + 9/10 = 2 9/10 m, so 2 full metres. (b) 29 tenths divided into strips of 4 tenths gives 7 strips (28 tenths) with 1 tenth, that is 1/10 m, left over.
s: Part (b): 7 strips and 1/10 m left over

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A strip of 38/100 m is longer than a strip of 4/10 m.
Reason (R): 4/10 m is the same as 40/100 m, and 38 hundredths is 2 hundredths less than 40 hundredths.
o: A is false but R is true.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.

questions.q: A screw is 4 8/10 cm long and another is 4 1/10 cm long. (a) Write the length of the first screw in tenths only. (b) By how many one-tenths is it longer than the second screw?
questions.a: (a) 4 8/10 = 40/10 + 8/10 = 48/10, i.e. 48 tenths. (b) The second is 41 tenths, so the first is longer by 48 - 41 = 7 tenths (7/10 cm).
s: Part (b): finds 41 tenths for the other and the gap of 7 tenths

questions.q: A shopkeeper in Ajmer lays 17 pieces of ribbon, each 1/10 m long, and then 9 pieces, each 1/100 m long, end to end. Which mixed form gives the total length?

Match each length in Column I with the same length written in hundredths only in Column II.
Column I: 1. 1 3/10 6/100 m   2. 2 5/100 m   3. 3/10 m and 6/100 m together   4. 1 8/10 m
Column II: a. 205/100 m   b. 136/100 m   c. 36/100 m   d. 180/100 m
A carpenter's note gives a plank as 34/10 m. His apprentice copies the length into other forms for the saw operator. Which copy changes the length?
questions.a: 34 one-hundredths of a metre
o: 3 m and 4 tenths of a metre

questions.q:
Consider the statements about lengths.
Statement 1: 41/10 is read 'forty-one tenths' and is the same as 4 1/10.
Statement 2: 2 6/100 m is the same length as 2 6/10 m, because both have 2 units and a 6.
Statement 3: 10 one-tenths make 1 unit, so 130/10 is 13 units.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only

questions.q: Arrange in increasing order: 38/10, 3 5/10, 3/10, 83/10. Say how you compared them.
questions.a: 3/10 < 3 5/10 < 38/10 < 83/10. Write each as a mixed form: 0 3/10, 3 5/10, 3 8/10, 8 3/10; compare the units first, and the tenths where the units tie.
s: Converts all four to a common form (units and tenths)

questions.q: On a tailor's tape every centimetre is divided into 10 equal parts. A button's left edge is at 4 7/10 cm and its right edge at 6 2/10 cm. What is the width of the button?
Imran says: '43/100 cm is longer than 4 3/10 cm, because 43 is more than 4 and 3.' Is he right? Explain with the units.
questions.a: No. 43/100 is 43 one-hundredths, which is less than 1 unit (it is not even half a unit). 4 3/10 is more than 4 units. So 4 3/10 cm is longer.
s: Gives the verdict that Imran is wrong
Shows 4 3/10 is more than 4 units so it is longer

questions.q:
For sports day at a school in Nagpur, Chhaya prepares medal ribbons. The gold ribbon is 1 3/10 6/100 m, the silver ribbon is 1 2/10 9/100 m and the bronze ribbon is 1 1/10 15/100 m. Every ribbon must be at least 1 3/10 m long to go round a medal neatly.
(a) Write the gold and silver ribbons in hundredths only.
(b) Which is longer, and by how many hundredths?
(c) Write the bronze ribbon with fewer than 10 hundredths in the last place.
(d) Which ribbons can Chhaya use without buying new ribbon? Give your reason.
questions.a: (a) Gold = 130 + 6 = 136/100; silver = 120 + 9 = 129/100. (b) Gold is longer by 7 hundredths. (c) 15 hundredths = 1 tenth + 5 hundredths, so bronze = 1 2/10 5/100 (125/100). (d) Needed length 1 3/10 m = 130/100. Only the gold ribbon (136) is at least 130; silver is 129 and bronze is 125, both short.
s: Part (d): compares each with 130 hundredths and says only gold can be used

questions.q:
Ramesh, a tailor in Jaipur, has three pieces of lace for a lehenga border: 2 7/10 m, 3 5/10 m and 1 8/10 m. The customer's border needs 8 1/10 m. The shop sells extra lace only as a 2/10 m cut (₹60 each) or as one 1 m piece (₹90). The customer may also order a matching dupatta trim that needs 5/10 m more.
(a) Write the 3 5/10 m piece in tenths only.
(b) Find the total of the three pieces in tenths.
(c) By how many tenths is the lace short of 8 1/10 m?
(d) The customer says she will probably order the trim as well. Compare buying 2/10 m cuts with buying the 1 m piece, in length and in cost, and decide.
questions.a: (a) 35/10. (b) 27 + 35 + 18 = 80 tenths = 8 m. (c) 81 - 80 = 1 tenth short. (d) With the trim the order needs 81 + 5 = 86 tenths, which is 6 tenths more than she has. That takes three 2/10 m cuts (₹180) but one 1 m piece (10 tenths, ₹90) covers it with 4 tenths to spare. If she orders the trim, buy the 1 m piece; if she orders only the border, a single 2/10 m cut (₹60) is enough.
s: Part (c): finds the shortage of 1 tenth
Part (d): needs 6 tenths with the trim, compares 3 cuts at ₹180 with one piece at ₹90, and states the conditional choice

questions.q: Create a real-life situation in which moving the decimal point of 2.5 one place to the right (to 25) would cause a problem. Say how many times the quantity changes.
questions.a: Any realistic story, e.g. a recipe or weighing: 2.5 kg of sugar is mistaken for 25 kg. The value becomes 10 times as large because each digit now sits in a place worth 10 times as much.
s: Gives a realistic situation using 2.5 and 25
States what the wrong reading means in that situation
States the quantity becomes 10 times bigger

questions.q: A student writes '4 units, 2 tenths and 9 thousandths' as 4.29 in her lab record. The correct decimal for this reading is
The digit 8 occurs in 38.4 and in 4.08. (a) Write the value of each 8 as a decimal. (b) How many times as much is the first 8 worth as the second? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) In 38.4 the 8 is 8 units = 8; in 4.08 it is 8 hundredths = 0.08. (b) The first is worth 100 times the second: units are 10 tenths and each tenth is 10 hundredths, so one place move of 2 steps is 10 x 10 = 100.
s: Part (b): says 100 times, with the two place steps (units to tenths to hundredths) as the reason

questions.q: Write each quantity as a decimal: (a) 3 ones, 4 tenths and 6 hundredths; (b) 2 tens and 8 tenths; (c) 5/100 and 3/10 together; (d) 4 hundreds and 7 hundredths. Then (e) read the decimal in (d) aloud.
questions.a: (a) 3.46. (b) 20.8. (c) 3/10 + 5/100 = 0.35. (d) 400.07, with zeros holding the tens, units and tenths places. (e) four hundred point zero seven.
s: Part (c): 0.35 by adding 3 tenths and 5 hundredths
Part (e): reads four hundred point zero seven

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The decimal 40.06 cannot be shortened to 40.6.
Reason (R): The zero in the tenths place holds that place, so the 6 stands for 6 hundredths; without the zero it would stand for 6 tenths.
o: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.a: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.q: True or False: The digit 3 in 0.43 is worth 100 times as much as the digit 3 in 0.403. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. In 0.43 the 3 is 3 hundredths (0.03); in 0.403 it is 3 thousandths (0.003). Each place is 10 times the place on its right, so the first 3 is worth 10 times the second, not 100 times.
s: Compares 0.03 with 0.003 and corrects 100 times to 10 times

questions.q: Mohan, a shopkeeper in Surat, wants to write 7 units and 5 hundredths on a bill but writes 7.5. By how much does the quantity he has written differ from the quantity he meant?
questions.a: It is 45 hundredths more

questions.q:
Match each description in Column I with the decimal in Column II.
Column I: 1. 3 units and 4 hundredths   2. 3 tens and 4 tenths   3. 3 tenths and 4 thousandths   4. 3 hundredths and 4 units
Column II: a. 30.4   b. 4.03   c. 0.304   d. 3.04
A pupil is told to record 'four point zero seven'. Sunil writes 4.7 and Tara writes 4.007. (a) Who is right? (b) Say which quantity each pupil actually wrote.
questions.a: (a) Neither: the correct record is 4.07. (b) Sunil's 4.7 is 4 units and 7 tenths; Tara's 4.007 is 4 units and 7 thousandths.
s: Part (a): says neither is right and writes 4.07
Part (b): 4.7 is 7 tenths and 4.007 is 7 thousandths

questions.q: Neha says: 'In 3.33 the first 3 is worth 10 times the middle 3, and the middle 3 is worth 10 times the last 3. So the first 3 is worth 20 times the last 3.' Is she right? Find the value of each 3 to decide.
questions.a: Partly right. The three 3s are worth 3, 0.3 and 0.03. The first is 10 times the middle (3 against 0.3) and the middle is 10 times the last (0.3 against 0.03), so both of her first two statements are true. But the first 3 is 10 x 10 = 100 times the last 3 (3 against 0.03), not 20 times: the steps multiply, they do not add.
s: Finds the values 3, 0.3 and 0.03 and confirms the two 10-times statements
Corrects 20 times to 100 times because 10 x 10, not 10 + 10

questions.q: Show that a single digit in the tenths place can never be worth as much as 1 unit, even for the largest digit 9.
questions.a: The largest digit is 9, and 9 tenths = 0.9. It takes 10 tenths to make 1 unit, so 9 tenths is 1 tenth short of a unit. A digit in the tenths place is therefore always less than 1 unit.
s: Takes the largest digit 9 in the tenths place and gets 0.9
States 10 tenths are needed for 1 unit
Concludes 0.9 is less than 1 so no tenths digit reaches 1 unit

questions.q: The digit 5 appears three times in the reading 5.505 kg. (a) Write the value of each of the three 5s as a decimal. (b) Add the values of the first and the last 5 and write the sum as a decimal.
questions.a: (a) The 5s are worth 5, 0.5 and 0.005. (b) 5 + 0.005 = 5.005, where the zeros in the tenths and hundredths places hold their places.
s: Part (b): sum 5.005 with the placeholder zeros

questions.q: A lab meter shows a reading of 7 units, 12 tenths and 5 hundredths. Written as a single decimal, the reading is ___.
(a) Write 234 hundredths as a decimal. (b) How many times bigger is 234 tenths than 234 hundredths?
questions.a: (a) 234 hundredths = 2.34. (b) 234 tenths = 23.4, which is 10 times 2.34.
s: Part (b): writes 234 tenths as 23.4 and finds the ratio 10

questions.q: A lab technician records a powder as 50.305 g, and a trainee writes it in expanded form to check the record. Which expanded form is correct?

A timing board shows three readings: 12.05 s, 12.5 s and 12.005 s. (a) Write the value of the digit 5 in each reading as a decimal. (b) Which 5 is worth the most, and how many times the 5 in 12.005 is it worth? (c) Which readings have a 0 in the tenths place? (d) Write 12.05 in the form tens, units, tenths, hundredths. (e) A pupil says the readings 12.5 s and 12.05 s are equal because they use the same digits. Use their difference to show she is wrong.
questions.a: (a) 0.05, 0.5 and 0.005. (b) The 5 in 12.5 (0.5) is worth the most: 0.5 is 100 times 0.005 (tenths to thousandths is two place steps, 10 x 10). (c) 12.05 and 12.005. (d) 1 ten, 2 units, 0 tenths, 5 hundredths. (e) 12.5 is 12 units and 5 tenths, 12.05 is 12 units and 5 hundredths; 12.50 - 12.05 = 0.45 s, so they are not equal.

questions.q: Karan converts 0.608 to the fraction form 6/10 + 8/100. (a) Find his error and write the correct sum of fractions. (b) Write 0.608 as a single fraction with denominator 1000.
questions.a: (a) The 8 is in the thousandths place, so 0.608 = 6/10 + 8/1000 (the hundredths place holds 0). (b) 600/1000 + 8/1000 = 608/1000.
s: Part (a): corrects 8/100 to 8/1000 because the hundredths digit is 0

questions.q:
Consider the statements about decimal notation.
Statement 1: In 0.274 the digit 7 stands for 7 tenths.
Statement 2: 7.05 means 7 x 1 + 5 x 1/100.
Statement 3: 234 tenths is written 23.4.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 and 3 only

questions.q: A pharmacist has two doses on her chart, 0.406 g and 0.46 g. By how much is the second dose larger than the first?
questions.a: 54 thousandths of a gram

questions.q:
A school lab in Chennai must choose a new measuring scale for a unit length. Scale P splits each unit into 4 equal parts and each quarter again into 4 equal parts. Scale Q splits each unit into 10 tenths and each tenth again into 10 hundredths. The lab's record sheet allows readings only as decimals with at most two places, its experiments need differences no coarser than 0.1 of a unit, and each class has only 30 minutes to read the scale (the more marks, the slower the reading).
(a) Write one smallest part of each scale as a fraction of the unit, and say which of the two is a decimal place.
(b) Which scale can show smaller differences, and how do you know?
(c) A reading on scale Q is 2 units, 3 tenths and 7 hundredths. Write it as a decimal and say by how much it is more than 2.3.
(d) Both scales meet the 0.1 need. Which should the lab choose, given the record sheet rule? Give one advantage and one drawback of your choice.
questions.a: (a) P: 4 x 4 = 16 parts, so one smallest part is 1/16 of a unit; Q: 10 x 10 = 100 parts, so 1/100. Only 1/100 is a decimal place (the hundredths place); 1/16 is not a tenth or a hundredth. (b) Q: its smallest part is 1/100 of a unit, smaller than 1/16, because a unit cut into 100 parts has finer parts than one cut into 16. (c) 2.37, which is 7 hundredths (0.07) more than 2.3. (d) Both meet the 0.1 need: 1/16 is smaller than 1/10 and 1/100 is smaller still. The record sheet decides it: choose Q. Advantage: every mark is a tenth or a hundredth, so each reading writes as a decimal with at most two places. Drawback: 100 marks per unit are slower to read in 30 minutes. Scale P is quicker (16 marks), but most of its marks (1/16, 3/16, 5/16 ...) are not tenths or hundredths, so they cannot be written within two places; only marks such as 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 can.
s: Part (a): 1/16 and 1/100, and says only 1/100 is a decimal place (hundredths)
Part (b): chooses Q because 1/100 is smaller than 1/16
Part (d): chooses Q using the two-place record rule, with one advantage and one drawback

questions.q:
In a school science fair in Pune, a group shows five heaps of rice. The first heap weighs 1 g, and each next heap is 10 times as heavy as the one before it. Their display table has a scale that can read only up to 12 kg.
(a) What does the third heap weigh in grams and in kilograms?
(b) What is the combined weight of the three lightest heaps in kilograms, as a decimal?
(c) In your answer to (b), which heap does the digit in the hundredths place stand for, and why?
(d) Can the group put all five heaps on the scale together? If they add a sixth heap by the same rule, will it fit on the scale? Give reasons.
questions.a: (a) 100 g = 0.1 kg. (b) 1 + 10 + 100 = 111 g = 0.111 kg. (c) The hundredths digit is 1; 1 hundredth of a kg is 0.01 kg = 10 g, so it stands for the 10 g heap. (d) All five: 1 + 10 + 100 + 1000 + 10000 = 11111 g = 11.111 kg, less than 12 kg, so they fit. The sixth heap is 100000 g = 100 kg, far above 12 kg, so it cannot be added.
s: Part (a): third heap is 100 g = 0.1 kg
Part (c): hundredths digit is 0.01 kg = 10 g, so the 10 g heap
Part (d): 11.111 kg < 12 kg so five fit; the sixth heap of 100 kg does not

questions.q: Kabir says: 'Writing 0.5 as 0.500 does not change it, but writing it as 0.05 does.' Is he right? Support your answer with place value.
questions.a: Yes. 0.5 is 5 tenths = 500 thousandths, and 0.500 is also 500 thousandths, so the extra zeros at the right end change nothing. 0.05 is 5 hundredths = 50 thousandths, because the zero put right after the point moves the 5 to a smaller place. The statement is true because it separates the two kinds of zero.
s: Gives the verdict that Kabir is right
Shows 0.05 is 50 thousandths because the zero was added just after the point

questions.q: True or False: A packet of 4.50 kg and a packet of 4.5 kg weigh the same, but a packet of 4.05 kg is 450 g lighter than the 4.50 kg packet. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: True. 4.50 kg and 4.5 kg are both 4 kg and 5 tenths, so they weigh the same. 4.05 kg has 0 tenths and 5 hundredths: 4.50 - 4.05 = 0.45 kg = 450 g (1 g = 0.001 kg, so 0.45 kg = 450 thousandths).
s: Equal forms 4.50 = 4.5, and works out the gap 0.45 kg = 450 g for 4.05

questions.q: (a) Write 64 ones, 8 tenths and 70 hundredths as a decimal. (b) Write the same value with exactly three digits after the point.
questions.a: (a) 70 hundredths = 7 tenths, so 64 + 0.8 + 0.7 = 65.5 (the same as 65.50). (b) With three digits after the point it is 65.500.
s: Part (a): regroups 70 hundredths as 7 tenths and gets 65.5

questions.q: A chemistry club pours 0.30 L, then 0.4 L, then 0.200 L of water into a jug whose capacity is 1 L. It then tries to pour in 0.15 L more. How much of that 0.15 L fits, and how much spills?
questions.a: 0.1 L fits and 0.05 L spills

questions.q: Show that 0.5, 0.05 and 0.005 cannot be made equal by adding zeros on the right of each.
questions.a: Written in thousandths: 0.5 = 500/1000, 0.05 = 50/1000, 0.005 = 5/1000. Adding zeros at the right only changes the number of places used; the three amounts stay 500, 50 and 5 thousandths, which are all different.
s: Writes the three in a common place (500, 50, 5 thousandths)
Notes added right-hand zeros do not change a value

questions.q: A lab report lists 0.002 g of a dye. One student copies it as 0.02 g and another as 0.0020 g. Compared with the report, which is correct?
questions.a: The first copy is 18 thousandths too large; the second is unchanged
o: The first copy is 18 thousandths too large; the second is unchanged
The first copy is 18 thousandths too large; the second is 10 times too large
The first copy is 2 thousandths too large; the second is unchanged
The first copy is 18 hundredths too large; the second is unchanged

questions.q: A notebook costs ₹6.8 at one shop, ₹6.80 at a second shop and ₹6.08 at a third shop. How much cheaper, in paise, is the notebook at the third shop than at the first?
o: 0 paise, since the shops show the same digits
questions.a: 72 paise

questions.q: Sonu says 0.2 can be written 0.20 and 0.200. Zara says adding zeros may change the value. (a) Write 0.2, 0.20, 0.200 and 0.02 in thousandths. (b) Who is right about the first three? (c) By how many thousandths does 0.2 exceed 0.02? (d) State what Zara should have said so that she is also right.
questions.a: (a) 200/1000, 200/1000, 200/1000 and 20/1000. (b) Sonu: all three are 2 tenths. (c) 200 - 20 = 180 thousandths. (d) Zeros added at the right end do not change the value; zeros added just after the point do (0.2 becomes 0.02).
s: Part (a): converts all four to thousandths correctly
Part (b): says Sonu is right for the first three
Part (d): states the condition: right end only, not after the point

questions.q: A digital scale in a lab always shows exactly three digits after the point. It is used to weigh 3.5 g, 0.35 g and 12 g of three powders, which are tipped into one pan, and then a fourth powder of 0.5 g is added. The scale can show at most 16.000 g without an overload warning. What does the display read, and does the warning appear?
questions.a: 16.350 g, and the warning appears

questions.q: Maya adds two quantities of juice and writes 0.7 L + 0.30 L = 0.37 L. (a) Find the slip in her working. (b) Write both numbers with two digits after the point and give the correct total.
questions.a: (a) She joined the digits 7 and 30 as if they were side by side, instead of adding like places: 0.7 is 7 tenths and 0.30 is 30 hundredths. (b) 0.70 + 0.30 = 1.00 L, since 70 + 30 = 100 hundredths.
s: Part (a): says tenths and hundredths were not added as like places
Part (b): rewrites as 0.70 + 0.30 and gets 1.00 L (100 hundredths)

questions.q: Jug A holds 0.6 L, jug B holds 0.60 L and jug C holds 0.06 L. (a) Both A and B are emptied into one bucket. How many hundredths of a litre are in the bucket? (b) By how many hundredths of a litre does the bucket's content exceed jug C?
questions.a: (a) 0.6 L = 0.60 L = 60 hundredths, so the bucket holds 60 + 60 = 120 hundredths (1.20 L). (b) Jug C holds 6 hundredths, so the excess is 120 - 6 = 114 hundredths.
s: Part (b): reads 0.06 as 6 hundredths and gets 114 hundredths

questions.q: From the numbers 3.6, 3.06, 0.306, 3.600, 3.60, 3.006 and 03.60: (a) list the numbers, other than 3.6 itself, that are equal to 3.6. (b) Of the three numbers that are not equal to 3.6, which is the smallest, and why?
questions.a: (a) 3.600, 3.60 and 03.60. (b) 0.306 is the smallest: it has 0 units, while 3.06 and 3.006 each have 3 units.
s: Part (b): picks 0.306 and gives the units-place reason

questions.q: (a) In the number 0.4050, of the two zeros that come after the 4, which can be dropped without changing its value, and which cannot? (b) Write the value in thousandths.
questions.a: (a) The zero at the right end can be dropped, giving 0.405. The zero between the 4 and the 5 cannot: 0.45 is 450 thousandths but 0.405 is 405 thousandths. (b) 405 thousandths (405/1000).
s: Part (a): drops only the right-end zero and explains why the middle zero stays

questions.q:
Consider the statements about zeros in decimals.
Statement 1: 0.5 L and 0.500 L are the same amount of liquid.
Statement 2: The zero in 0.05 can be dropped to give 0.5 without changing the value.
Statement 3: A weight of 3.070 kg is equal to 3.07 kg.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only

questions.q: A grocer in Indore labels five rice packets in kg: 2.50, 2.5, 2.05, 2.500 and 0.25. (a) Which labels show the same weight? (b) How many different weights are there? (c) List the different weights from lightest to heaviest. (d) By how many hundredths of a kg is 2.5 heavier than 2.05?
The depth of a pond is recorded in metres as 1.30 on Monday, 1.3 on Tuesday and 1.03 on Wednesday. Which statement about the three days is correct?
o: Monday and Tuesday had the same depth, and Wednesday was 27 hundredths of a metre less
All three days had the same depth, since each reading has 1, 3 and a 0
Tuesday and Wednesday had the same depth, and Monday was 27 hundredths more
Monday was 3 hundredths deeper than Tuesday
questions.a: Monday and Tuesday had the same depth, and Wednesday was 27 hundredths of a metre less

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The sum 0.40 + 0.4 + 0.400 is 1.2.
Reason (R): Each zero added at the right end of a decimal moves its digits to a smaller place, so 0.400 is smaller than 0.4.
questions.a: A is true but R is false.
o: A is true but R is false.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: A lab runs an experiment three times and uses 0.250 kg, 0.25 kg and 0.5 kg of salt. The total used is ___ hundredths of a kilogram.
Write three different decimals that all equal 4 tenths, and one similar-looking decimal that does not. Say why the last one is different.
questions.a: 0.4, 0.40 and 0.400 are all 4 tenths. 0.04 looks similar but is 4 hundredths, one tenth of 0.4, because the 4 has moved one place to the right.
s: Gives three valid equal forms of 4 tenths
Explains with place value that it is 4 hundredths

questions.q:
Aarav wants a geometry box from one of four shops in his Delhi market. The same make is priced Shop A ₹24.50, Shop B ₹24.5, Shop C ₹24.05 and Shop D ₹2.45. He has ₹25 and can walk to only one shop. His mother has warned him that a price board is sometimes written wrongly by a helper, and that he must not come home without the box.
(a) Which two shops charge exactly the same price?
(b) By how many paise is Shop C cheaper than Shop A?
(c) Compare the digits of Shop D's price with Shop A's. Where has the point moved, and what part of Shop A's price is Shop D's?
(d) Shop D's board may be a misprint or a real offer. Decide which shop Aarav should walk to, and give your reason.
questions.a: (a) Shops A and B (24.50 = 24.5). (b) A is 2450 paise and C is 2405 paise, so C is 45 paise cheaper. (c) D uses the same digits 245 as A with the point one place to the left, so D's price (245 paise) is one tenth of A's (2450 paise). (d) A price exactly a tenth of the others may be a misprint, so the safe choice is Shop C (cheapest of the reliable ones, 45 paise below A and within ₹25); going to D is a gamble that pays off only if the offer is real. Any choice is accepted if it weighs the risk.
s: Part (c): same digits, point one place left, one tenth of A's price
Part (d): chooses a shop and weighs the misprint risk against the saving

questions.q:
A cooperative store in Kochi packs rice in bags labelled 1.25 kg. An inspector weighs four bags with a scale that shows three digits after the point, and records 1.250 kg, 1.25 kg, 1.025 kg and 1.205 kg. A bag passes only if its weight equals the label exactly, and the store must re-pack any bag that fails before the van leaves at noon.
(a) Which of the four recorded weights are equal to 1.25 kg?
(b) Write 1.25 kg with three digits after the point and say how many thousandths of a kg the part after the point has.
(c) By how many thousandths does the heavier of the two failing bags exceed the lighter one?
(d) The store re-packs first the failing bag that is further from the label. Which bag is that, and by how many thousandths is it off?
questions.a: (a) 1.250 and 1.25. (b) 1.250; 250 thousandths. (c) 1.205 - 1.025 = 180 thousandths. (d) 1.025 is 225 thousandths short and 1.205 is 45 thousandths short, so 1.025 is further away and is re-packed first, 225 thousandths off.
s: Part (c): finds the gap 180 thousandths between 1.205 and 1.025
Part (d): finds shortfalls 225 and 45 thousandths and chooses 1.025 first

questions.q: Rani says: '5.37 is smaller than 5.4 although it has more digits, so a decimal with fewer digits after the point is always the larger one.' Is she right? Test both parts of her claim.
questions.a: Partly right. The first part is true: 5.37 < 5.4 because the tenths are 3 and 4, so the first difference decides. The word 'always' is wrong: 5.41 has more digits than 5.4 and is larger, since 5.41 > 5.40. The number of digits never decides.
s: Gives the verdict that she is only partly right
Gives a counter-example such as 5.41 > 5.4 to defeat 'always'

questions.q: Two lab balances read 3.456 g and 3.465 g for the same sample. The two readings first differ at the hundredths digit, and the gap between them is ___ thousandths of a gram.

Write two decimals A and B such that A has more digits after the point than B and A is smaller than B. Then write two decimals C and D where C has more digits and is larger. Explain what decides each pair.
questions.a: For example A = 5.382 and B = 5.4: A has more digits but is smaller since the tenths 3 < 4. And C = 5.41 and D = 5.4: C has more digits and is larger since 5.41 > 5.40. The first place where the digits differ decides, not the number of digits.
s: Gives a valid pair where more digits means smaller
Gives a valid pair where more digits means larger
Explains the first differing place decides

questions.q: True or False: 0.808 is greater than 0.88 because 808 is greater than 88. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. Compare place by place from the left: the units (0) and the tenths (8) are equal, and at the hundredths 0.808 has 0 while 0.88 has 8. So 0.808 is less than 0.88. The number of digits after the point does not decide.
s: Compares from the highest place and finds the hundredths decide (0 against 8)

questions.q: A surveyor's chart shows the segment from 6.7 to 6.8 divided into 10 equal parts. Marker P is three marks to the left of 6.8 and marker Q is two marks to the right of 6.7. How far apart are P and Q?
A code uses the digits 2, 7 and 5, each exactly once, after the point in 4.___ ___ ___. (a) Write the greatest and the smallest such decimal. (b) Find the gap between them in thousandths.
questions.a: (a) Greatest 4.752, smallest 4.257 (put the largest digit in the highest place for the greatest and the smallest digit there for the smallest). (b) 4.752 - 4.257 = 0.495, i.e. 495 thousandths.

questions.q: Four parcels weigh 7.9 kg, 7.099 kg, 7.09 kg and 17.009 kg. A careless clerk believes 'more digits after the point means heavier' and loads 7.099 kg first. Which parcel is truly the heaviest?

In a javelin event at a school meet in Bhopal, five throws (in metres) are 31.38, 31.083, 31.8, 30.99 and 31.308. (a) Rank them from longest to shortest. (b) Which throw won, and which was second? (c) By how many hundredths of a metre did the winner beat the second place? (d) The school record is 31.4 m. A throw is accepted as matching the record if it is at most 0.02 m below it. Which of the five throws match or beat the record?
questions.a: (a) 31.8, 31.38, 31.308, 31.083, 30.99. (b) 31.8 won; 31.38 was second. (c) 31.80 - 31.38 = 0.42, i.e. 42 hundredths. (d) 31.8 beats it; 31.38 is 31.40 - 31.38 = 0.02 below, which is allowed, so it matches. 31.308 is 0.092 below, so it does not; the others are lower still. So 31.8 and 31.38.
s: Part (d): 31.8 beats and 31.38 is exactly 0.02 below, so both count

questions.q: A lab notes the masses 4.38 g, 4.308 g and 4.380 g. (a) Which two are equal? (b) Which is the smallest, and at which place do you first see that it is smaller?
questions.a: (a) 4.38 g and 4.380 g are equal (the trailing zero adds nothing). (b) 4.308 g is the smallest: the units and tenths tie (4 and 3), and at the hundredths it has 0 against 8.
s: Part (b): picks 4.308 and names the hundredths place (0 against 8)

questions.q: Arrange these masses in descending order: 8.304 g, 8.34 g, 8.043 g, 8.4 g, 8.399 g. Name the digit that decided between the first two.
questions.a: 8.4 > 8.399 > 8.34 > 8.304 > 8.043. All have 8 units; the tenths digits are 4, 3, 3, 3, 0, so 8.4 is greatest. Between the first two, 8.4 and 8.399, the tenths digits 4 and 3 decide (4 > 3), whatever follows.
s: Names the deciding digit for the first two (tenths 4 versus 3)

questions.q: A number line from 0 to 1 is divided into 10 equal parts, and each part is divided again into 10 equal smaller parts. (a) Between which two tenth marks does 0.37 lie, and which small mark of that part is it? (b) How many small marks lie strictly between 0.37 and 0.52?
questions.a: (a) 0.37 is 3 tenths and 7 hundredths, so it lies between the marks 0.3 and 0.4, on the 7th small mark. (b) The small marks are the hundredths 0.38, 0.39, ..., 0.51. That is 51 - 37 = 14 marks.
s: Part (a): between 0.3 and 0.4 on the 7th small mark
Part (b): counts the hundredths from 0.38 to 0.51 and gets 14

questions.q:
Assertion (A): 0.35 is greater than 0.4 because 35 is greater than 4.
Reason (R): Decimals are compared place by place, starting from the highest place value.
questions.a: A is false but R is true.
o: A is false but R is true.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.q: On a number line, point P is at the 7th mark when the gap from 3 to 4 is cut into 10 equal parts, and then at the 4th mark when the gap from 3.7 to 3.8 is cut into 10 equal parts. (a) Write the decimal for P. (b) Is P greater or less than 3.8, and by how many hundredths?
questions.a: (a) P = 3.7 + 4 hundredths = 3.74. (b) P is less than 3.8; 3.80 - 3.74 = 0.06, which is 6 hundredths.
s: Part (a): reads the two zooms to get 3.74
Part (b): says less than 3.8 and finds the gap of 6 hundredths

questions.q: Ishaan locates 6.274 on a number line by magnifying one segment at a time. His first two segments are 6 to 7 and then 6.2 to 6.3. Which describes the third segment and where 6.274 lies in it?
questions.a: 6.27 to 6.28, with 6.274 at the fourth mark after 6.27
o: 6.27 to 6.28, with 6.274 at the fourth mark after 6.27
6.27 to 6.28, with 6.274 at the fourth mark before 6.28
6.2 to 6.3 again, with 6.274 at the 74th mark
6.27 to 6.28, with 6.274 at the seventh mark after 6.27

questions.q: Show that no decimal with only one digit after the point lies strictly between 3.6 and 3.7. Then name a decimal with two digits that does.
questions.a: One-digit decimals are whole numbers of tenths: 3.6, 3.7 differ by exactly 1 tenth, so no whole number of tenths lies strictly between them. Splitting the gap into 10 equal parts gives hundredths such as 3.65, which lies between them.
s: Concludes no one-digit decimal lies between them
Gives a two-digit example such as 3.65

questions.q:
Match each pair of readings in Column I with the gap between the two numbers, in thousandths, in Column II.
Column I: 1. 3.456 and 3.465   2. 5.37 and 5.4   3. 6.45 and 6.54   4. 9.2 and 8.3
Column II: a. 9 thousandths   b. 30 thousandths   c. 90 thousandths   d. 900 thousandths

Consider the statements about comparing decimals.
Statement 1: Of 4.07, 4.7 and 4.007, the greatest is 4.7.
Statement 2: The gap between 3.65 and 3.7 is 5 hundredths.
Statement 3: 5.38 is greater than 5.4 because 38 is greater than 4.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 2 only

questions.q: A chef arranges four spice jars by weight, lightest first, and notes the gap between the heaviest and the lightest. Their weights are 2.5 g, 2.55 g, 2.05 g and 2.505 g. Which order and gap are correct?

A student zooms into the number line between 6.4 and 6.5. (a) Name one two-digit decimal strictly between 6.4 and 6.5. (b) How many two-digit decimals lie strictly between 6.4 and 6.5? (c) Name one three-digit decimal strictly between 6.45 and 6.46. (d) Is there a decimal strictly between 6.45 and 6.46? Explain what this shows about zooming in.
questions.a: (a) Any of 6.41, 6.42, ..., 6.49, for example 6.45. (b) 9 of them (6.41 to 6.49). (c) Any of 6.451 to 6.459, for example 6.455. (d) Yes. Cut the gap of one hundredth into 10 equal parts to get thousandths; this can be repeated, so between any two decimals there is always another and zooming never runs out of room.
s: Part (a): a valid two-digit decimal such as 6.45
Part (c): a valid three-digit decimal such as 6.455
Part (d): says yes and explains that the gap can be cut into 10 equal parts again

questions.q:
A school weather club in Chennai records rainfall each day in cm: Monday 12.305, Tuesday 12.35, Wednesday 12.053 and Thursday 12.5. The readings come from one rain gauge that shows three digits after the point. The club will send a flood warning to the municipal office for any day on which the rainfall is more than 12.35 cm, and not otherwise.
(a) Which day had the heaviest rain and which the lightest?
(b) Monday's and Tuesday's readings both lie in the same tenth-segment of the number line. Name its end points.
(c) By how many thousandths of a cm does Tuesday's reading exceed Monday's?
(d) On which days should the club send a warning? Justify your answer for Tuesday.
questions.a: (a) Heaviest: Thursday (12.5); lightest: Wednesday (12.053). (b) 12.3 and 12.4. (c) 12.350 - 12.305 = 45 thousandths. (d) Only Thursday: 12.5 > 12.35. Tuesday is exactly 12.35, which is not more than 12.35, so no warning for Tuesday under the stated rule.
s: Part (d): warns for Thursday only and justifies Tuesday as equal, not more

questions.q:
At a school sports day in Mysuru, five girls ran the 100 m race. Their times in seconds were Aisha 14.28, Bhavna 14.082, Chitra 14.8, Dolly 14.208 and Esha 14.265. The district team takes the two fastest runners who ran under 14.25 seconds. One reserve may also be named, and the rules allow a reserve only if her time is within 0.02 seconds above 14.25.
(a) Arrange the girls from the fastest (smallest time) to the slowest.
(b) By how many thousandths of a second did the winner beat the runner-up?
(c) Which girls ran under 14.25 seconds, and by how many thousandths does Esha miss that mark?
(d) Who should be the two team members and who, if anyone, may be the reserve? Justify with the differences.
questions.a: (a) Bhavna 14.082, Dolly 14.208, Esha 14.265, Aisha 14.28, Chitra 14.8. (b) 14.208 - 14.082 = 126 thousandths. (c) Bhavna and Dolly. Esha misses by 14.265 - 14.25 = 15 thousandths. (d) The team is Bhavna and Dolly. Esha is 15 thousandths (0.015 s) above the mark, within the 0.02 s allowed, so she may be reserve; Aisha is 30 thousandths (0.030 s) above, which is more than 0.02, so she cannot.
s: Part (a): orders Bhavna, Dolly, Esha, Aisha, Chitra
Part (c): Bhavna and Dolly under 14.25, Esha misses by 15 thousandths
Part (d): team Bhavna and Dolly; reserve Esha (0.015 within 0.02), not Aisha (0.030)

questions.q: (a) Write 2480 g in kilograms. (b) Is that more or less than 2.5 kg, and by how many grams?
s: Part (b): less than 2.5 kg by 20 g

questions.q: A billing machine accepts only kilograms. Ravi buys 250 g of ginger, 1.5 kg of onions and 380 g of garlic in one bill. The shop gives free delivery on 2 kg or more. What total must be typed, and how does it compare with the free-delivery limit?
o: 2.13 kg, which is 130 g above the limit
2.13 kg, which is 13 g above the limit
1.88 kg, which is 120 g below the limit
4.38 kg, which is 2.38 kg above the limit
questions.a: 2.13 kg, which is 130 g above the limit

questions.q: True or False: ₹6.5 means 6 rupees and 5 paise. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. The digit 5 sits in the tenths place, so it is 5 tenths of a rupee. One rupee is 100 paise, so a tenth is 10 paise and 5 tenths is 50 paise. ₹6.5 is 6 rupees and 50 paise (₹6.50).
s: Shows 5 tenths of a rupee = 50 paise, so the amount is ₹6.50

questions.q: A school stationery stall in Ranchi prices items as: pen 750 paise, notebook ₹18.5, ruler 1250 paise, eraser ₹4.05 and sharpener 305 paise. (a) Write every price in rupees as a decimal. (b) Which item is the costliest and which the cheapest? (c) How many paise is the notebook, and how many paise dearer is it than the ruler?
questions.a: (a) pen ₹7.5, notebook ₹18.5, ruler ₹12.5, eraser ₹4.05, sharpener ₹3.05. (b) Costliest: notebook (18.5); cheapest: sharpener (3.05). (c) 18.5 = 1850 paise; 1850 - 1250 = 600 paise dearer.

questions.q: Radha's mother lists sugar 640 g, ghee 0.48 kg, rice 2.5 kg, salt 250 g and tea 95 g. (a) Write the three items given in grams in kilograms. (b) Arrange all five items from lightest to heaviest. (c) What is the combined weight of the sugar and the salt, in kilograms?
questions.a: (a) sugar 0.64 kg, salt 0.25 kg, tea 0.095 kg (ghee and rice are already in kg). (b) tea, salt, ghee, sugar, rice. (c) 0.64 + 0.25 = 0.89 kg.
s: Part (b): tea, salt, ghee, sugar, rice

questions.q: A long jumper clears 3.25 m and her friend clears 318 cm. (a) Write 3.25 m in centimetres. (b) Who jumped farther, and by how many millimetres?
questions.a: (a) 3.25 m = 300 cm + 25 cm = 325 cm. (b) 325 cm > 318 cm, so the first jumper is farther, by 7 cm = 70 mm.
s: Part (b): names the first jumper and finds 7 cm = 70 mm

questions.q: A photocopy shop near a school in Bhopal charges 75 paise a page. (a) Write 75 paise in rupees. (b) A teacher gets 640 pages copied. What does she pay in rupees?
Rani converts 6 g to kilograms and writes 0.06 kg; she converts 6 mm to centimetres and writes 0.6 cm. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: Only the second conversion is right; 6 g is 0.006 kg
o: Only the second conversion is right; 6 g is 0.006 kg
Only the first conversion is right; 6 mm is 0.06 cm

questions.q: A pencil is 4.3 cm long and its refill is 87 mm long. (a) Write the pencil's length in millimetres. (b) Write the refill's length in metres and say by how many millimetres the pencil is shorter than the refill.
questions.a: (a) 4.3 cm is 4 cm and 3 tenths of a cm; each tenth of a cm is 1 mm, so 4 cm 3 mm = 40 mm + 3 mm = 43 mm. (b) 87 mm = 87/1000 m = 0.087 m. The pencil is 87 - 43 = 44 mm shorter than the refill.
s: Part (b): 0.087 m and the gap of 44 mm

questions.q: A parcel weighs 0.746 kg. A 250 g card and a 4 g sheet are added to it. The total weight is ___ g.
A pattern book lists a sleeve as 158 mm and a trouser leg as 1.58 m. Written in the same unit, the trouser leg is longer than the sleeve by
A shopkeeper says a sack of 2.5 kg weighs 250 g. Show that this cannot be right and give its weight in grams.
questions.a: 250 g is 250/1000 = 0.25 kg, which is a tenth of 2.5 kg. 2.5 kg = 2 kg + 0.5 kg = 2000 g + 500 g = 2500 g, so the sack cannot weigh 250 g.

questions.q: Make up a real-life situation in which a length of 58 cm has to be written in metres. Give the length in metres and show why that is correct.
questions.a: Any suitable story, e.g. a shelf board 58 cm long that a form wants in metres. 58 cm = 58/100 m = 50/100 + 8/100 = 0.58 m.
s: Gives 0.58 m with the hundredths reason

questions.q: A 1970s bill from a shop in Madurai lists 3 bananas at 25 paise each and one coconut at ₹0.85. Mother pays with a ₹2 coin. How much change should she get, written in rupees?

Reason (R): 1 mm is one hundredth of a centimetre, so 7 mm is 7 hundredths of a centimetre.
o: A is true but R is false.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

Consider the statements about unit conversion.
Statement 1: 1 mm is 0.01 cm.
Statement 2: 5 g is 0.05 kg.
Statement 3: 2340 g is 2.34 kg.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 3 only

questions.q:
Work out each calculation in Column I and match it with the same quantity, written in a different unit, in Column II.
Column I: 1. 1.2 kg + 250 g   2. 2 m - 110 cm   3. ₹1 - 35 paise   4. 4 cm 3 mm + 2.7 cm
Column II: a. ₹0.65   b. 0.07 m   c. 1450 g   d. 90 cm
A sheet of paper is 0.1 mm thick. (a) Write the thickness in centimetres using fractions of a centimetre. (b) How many such sheets stacked make a pile exactly 1 cm high?
questions.a: (a) 1 mm = 1/10 cm, and 0.1 mm is one tenth of that, 1/100 cm = 0.01 cm. (b) 1 cm = 10 mm = 100 tenths of a millimetre, and each sheet is 1 tenth of a millimetre, so 100 sheets.
s: Part (a): 1 mm = 1/10 cm so 0.1 mm = 1/100 cm = 0.01 cm
Part (b): 1 cm holds 100 tenths of a mm, so 100 sheets

questions.q: Gita says: '1 cm is 0.01 m, so 3 cm is 0.03 m and 30 cm is 0.3 m. In the same way 3 mm is 0.03 m.' Is she right? Check each of the three statements.
questions.a: Partly right. 3 cm = 3/100 m = 0.03 m and 30 cm = 30/100 m = 0.3 m are correct. 3 mm is not 0.03 m: 1 m = 1000 mm, so 3 mm = 3/1000 m = 0.003 m. She used hundredths where thousandths are needed.
s: Gives the verdict that she is only partly right
Confirms 3 cm = 0.03 m and 30 cm = 0.3 m using hundredths of a metre

questions.q:
Grandfather in Madurai remembers prices from the 1970s: a masala dosa cost 50 paise, a banana 25 paise and a kilogram of rice ₹2.45. One day he had exactly ₹3. He had to buy the rice, and he also wanted either the dosa or the banana. He needed to keep at least 20 paise for the bus fare home.
(a) Write the dosa and banana prices in rupees.
(b) Write the price of a kilogram of rice in paise.
(c) How much is left from ₹3 after buying the rice?
(d) Which treat can he afford, and why? Say how much remains in each case.
questions.a: (a) ₹0.50 and ₹0.25. (b) 245 paise. (c) 3.00 - 2.45 = ₹0.55 (55 paise). (d) Rice + dosa costs ₹2.95, leaving ₹0.05, which is less than the 20 paise needed for the bus. Rice + banana costs ₹2.70, leaving ₹0.30, which is enough. So he can afford the banana but not the dosa, even though the dosa is the bigger treat.
s: Part (d): dosa leaves 5 paise (too little), banana leaves 30 paise, so the banana

questions.q:
A museum in Kolkata is putting three small specimens in a display slot that is 2.0 cm wide. Its labels give: a hummingbird egg 1.3 cm long and 0.9 cm wide; a Philippine Goby about 0.9 cm long; and a Wolfi octopus, whose typical size ranges from 1 cm to 2.5 cm.
(a) Write the length and width of the egg in millimetres.
(b) Write the largest size of the octopus in metres.
(c) By how many millimetres is the egg's length less than the slot's width?
(d) Which specimens are certain to fit in the slot, and what should the museum do about the third?
questions.a: (a) 13 mm long and 9 mm wide. (b) 2.5 cm = 0.025 m. (c) The slot is 20 mm; 7 mm more than the egg's length. (d) The egg (13 mm) and the goby (9 mm) fit. The octopus may be up to 25 mm, which is more than 20 mm, so it may not fit; the museum should measure its actual specimen first or use a wider slot.
s: Part (d): egg and goby fit; octopus up to 25 mm may not, so measure it or widen the slot

questions.q: Find 63.402 - 48.759. Show where you have to borrow.
questions.a: Thousandths: 2 < 9, so borrow from the hundredths; the 0 there borrows 1 tenth first (tenths 4 become 3), giving hundredths 9 and thousandths 12. Then 12 - 9 = 3, 9 - 5 = 4, and tenths 3 - 7 borrows 1 unit (13 - 7 = 6). Units 2 - 8 borrows 1 ten (12 - 8 = 4), then 5 - 4 = 1. Result: 14.643.
s: Shows the borrowing across thousandths, hundredths, tenths and units

questions.q: A school in Vadodara has a storage drum that holds 600 litres and starts empty. In the morning 346.8 litres were pumped into it and in the afternoon 189.65 litres more. During the evening 275.4 litres were drawn out of the same drum. (a) How much was pumped in altogether? (b) How much water remains in the drum? (c) A tanker then pours 45.5 litres into the same drum. How much water is in the drum now, and how much more can it still take before it is full?
A farm sells 56.4 kg of beans on Saturday and 48.75 kg on Sunday. (a) Find the total sold. (b) Of this, 38.6 kg were bought by a hotel. How much was bought by others?
A student works out 12.65 - 4.8 and gets 8.25. Show by checking with addition that this cannot be right, then give the correct difference and the likely slip.
questions.a: If 8.25 were right, 8.25 + 4.8 would be 12.65, but 8.25 + 4.80 = 13.05. So 8.25 is wrong. The correct difference is 12.65 - 4.80 = 7.85. The slip: in the tenths column 6 - 8 cannot be done, so she took 8 - 6 = 2 and never borrowed from the units.
s: Says 13.05 is not 12.65 so 8.25 is impossible
Gives the correct difference 7.85 and names the borrowing slip

Reason (R): Taking a decimal between 0 and 1 away from 40 always leaves a result between 39 and 40.
o: A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.

questions.q: True or False: To add 7.5 and 0.25 in columns we should line up the last digits of the two numbers. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. The decimal points must be one below the other, so tenths sit under tenths and hundredths under hundredths. Writing 7.50 + 0.25 gives 7.75; lining up the last digits would add 5 tenths to 5 hundredths.
s: Says the decimal points are aligned and shows 7.50 + 0.25 = 7.75

questions.q: A rope is 1.5 m long. A tailor ties on a 35 cm strip and then an 8 mm cord. (a) Write 35 cm and 8 mm in metres. (b) Find the total length in metres.
s: Part (b): aligns the points and gets 1.858 m

questions.q: (a) Add 8.364 and 0.678, and check that your answer lies in the range given by the whole-number parts. (b) Using the result of (a) only, with no new column work, write the values of 9.042 - 0.678 and 9.042 - 8.364 and say why they follow.
questions.a: (a) 8.364 + 0.678 = 9.042; the whole parts give 8 + 0 = 8, so the sum lies between 8 and 10, and 9.042 is inside. (b) 9.042 - 0.678 = 8.364 and 9.042 - 8.364 = 0.678, because subtraction undoes the addition: taking one addend away from the sum leaves the other.
s: Part (a): 9.042 with the range 8 to 10 checked
Part (b): 8.364 and 0.678, with the add-back reason

questions.q: A cloth merchant in Surat buys rolls of 14.625 m, 8.75 m and 11.4 m and cuts 27.5 m for a uniform order. His assistant writes: '14.625 + 8.75 = 23.375; 23.375 + 11.4 = 34.775; 34.775 - 27.5 = 7.375.' (a) Check the total length. (b) Find the line in which the assistant went wrong and give the correct result. (c) Show how adding back catches the mistake. (d) By how much is the longest roll longer than the shortest?
questions.a: (a) 34.775 m, so the first two lines are right. (b) The last line is wrong: 34.775 - 27.500 = 7.275 m, not 7.375 (he is 1 tenth too high, a borrowing slip in the tenths). (c) 7.375 + 27.5 = 34.875, which is not 34.775, so 7.375 cannot be right; 7.275 + 27.5 = 34.775. (d) 14.625 - 8.75 = 5.875 m.
s: Part (b): finds the last line wrong and gives 7.275 m
Part (c): adds back to get 34.875 and compares with 34.775

questions.q: Imran's mother has 12.4 m of cloth. She uses 6.7 m for curtains and then 2.65 m for cushion covers. She wants a table runner 3.1 m long from what is left. Which statement is correct?
o: 3.05 m is left, which is 0.05 m short of the runner
3.05 m is left, which leaves 0.05 m spare after the runner
3.15 m is left, so the runner fits with 0.05 m spare
2.15 m is left, which is 0.95 m short of the runner
questions.a: 3.05 m is left, which is 0.05 m short of the runner

questions.q: Write a real-life word problem that is solved by finding 15.3 - 8.75, and solve it.
questions.a: Any suitable story, e.g. a tank holds 15.3 L and 8.75 L is used. Answer: 15.30 - 8.75 = 6.55 L, found by writing 15.3 as 15.30 and borrowing across the hundredths and tenths.

questions.q: At a farmers' market in Nashik, Sarita buys 3.75 kg of tomatoes, 2.5 kg of onions and 0.45 kg of green chillies. Her bag holds at most 7 kg. What is the weight now, and can she add 0.5 kg of ginger?
questions.a: 6.7 kg, and no because it would reach 7.2 kg
o: 6.7 kg, and no because it would reach 7.2 kg
6.7 kg, and yes because it would reach 6.75 kg

questions.q:
Consider the statements.
Statement 1: To add 25 and 4.6 we may write 25 as 25.0 and put the points in one line.
Statement 2: 0.64 + 0.07 = 0.71.
Statement 3: 8.3 - 8.03 = 0.3.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 2 only

questions.q: A pupil adds 17.4 + 6.85 + 0.09 in columns but puts the 9 of 0.09 under the tenths digits, so her total is 25.15. The correct total is ___.
A 10 L water can springs two leaks: first 0.07 L drips out, then 0.15 L more. Ria says 'only 0.15 - 0.07 = 0.08 L is lost, so 9.92 L is left.' Which statement is correct?
o: Ria subtracted the two leaks instead of adding them; 9.78 L is left
Ria misplaced the decimal point; 9.88 L is left
Ria is right, 9.92 L is left
Ria added when she should have subtracted; 10.22 L is left
questions.a: Ria subtracted the two leaks instead of adding them; 9.78 L is left

questions.q: A chemist has 52.806 g of salt and uses 25.9 g in one experiment. Her notebook says 52.806 - 25.9 = 52.547 g is left. Which statement is correct?
o: Wrong: the range is 26 to 28; 26.906 g is left (she used 0.259)
Right: the whole parts give a range of 52 to 54, which contains 52.547
Wrong: the range is 26 to 28, and 27.906 g is left; she forgot a borrow
Right: 52.806 - 25.9 keeps the 52 and only the .806 changes
questions.a: Wrong: the range is 26 to 28; 26.906 g is left (she used 0.259)

questions.q: Neha claims: '25 - 9.7 = 16.7, because 25 - 9 = 16 and the .7 just stays.' Is her claim right? Test it, and give the correct answer.
questions.a: No. The 0.7 is being taken away as well, not kept. Write 25 as 24 and 10 tenths: 10 tenths - 7 tenths = 3 tenths, and 24 - 9 = 15, so 25 - 9.7 = 15.3. Her answer 16.7 is wrong; check: 15.3 + 9.7 = 25.
s: Names the error: the 0.7 must also be subtracted
Works out 15.3 by regrouping 25 as 24 and 10 tenths

questions.q: Add 19.99 and 6.01. Show the carries across the decimal point, and say why the answer is a whole number.
questions.a: Hundredths 9 + 1 = 10 (write 0, carry 1 tenth); tenths 9 + 0 + 1 = 10 (write 0, carry 1 unit); units 9 + 6 + 1 = 16 (write 6, carry 1 ten); tens 1 + 0 + 1 = 2. Sum = 26.00. The decimal parts 0.99 and 0.01 together make exactly 1.
s: Shows the carries from hundredths and tenths across the point, and on to the tens

questions.q: A bamboo shoot in a school garden grew 0.478 m in the first week and 0.7 m in the second. The class wants its total growth after three weeks to be exactly 1.6 m. How much must it grow in the third week?

A patient at a clinic in Lucknow has his temperature (in °C) recorded on a chart: 39.2 at 8 a.m., 38.65 at 2 p.m., 37.9 at 8 p.m. and 37.45 the next morning at 8 a.m. The doctor will discharge him only if the temperature has fallen by more than 1.5 °C from its highest reading and the latest reading is below 37.5 °C.
(a) By how much did the temperature fall between 8 a.m. and 2 p.m.?
(b) What is the total fall from the highest reading to the latest reading?
(c) By how much is the latest reading below 37.5 °C?
(d) Should he be discharged? Justify using your answers, and say how close the figures are to the limits.
questions.a: (a) 39.2 - 38.65 = 0.55 °C. (b) 39.2 - 37.45 = 1.75 °C. (c) 37.5 - 37.45 = 0.05 °C. (d) Yes. The fall of 1.75 is more than 1.5 (by 0.25) and 37.45 is below 37.5 (by 0.05). Both conditions are met, but narrowly, so the doctor may prefer one more reading.
s: Part (d): discharges, citing both conditions and the narrow margins

questions.q:
The Class 7 teachers in a school in Coimbatore collect picnic money: Section A pays ₹3,480.75 and Section B pays ₹2,915.50. The bus costs ₹4,250.25. The caterer quotes ₹2,198.40 for the standard lunch (with sweets) or ₹2,139.85 for a smaller menu (no sweets). The principal says she will add ₹60.00 if asked in writing today.
(a) What is the total collected?
(b) How much is left after paying for the bus?
(c) How much would the standard lunch cost beyond that money?
(d) Should the teachers ask the principal for the ₹60.00 and order the standard lunch, or order the smaller menu? Give your reason with the money left in each case.
questions.a: (a) 3,480.75 + 2,915.50 = ₹6,396.25. (b) 6,396.25 - 4,250.25 = ₹2,146.00. (c) 2,198.40 - 2,146.00 = ₹52.40. (d) With the principal's ₹60.00 the standard lunch is affordable and ₹7.60 is left. The smaller menu needs no request and leaves ₹6.15. Either can be defended: the standard lunch gives sweets for ₹52.40 of outside money; the smaller menu keeps the class independent of outside money.
s: Part (d): compares ₹7.60 left with the principal's help against ₹6.15 left without it, and justifies a choice

questions.q: Two pupils write 47.3 - 18.8 as 31.5 and as 29.5. The range from the whole-number parts, 28 to 30, rules out only one of them, yet the other is also wrong. The correct difference is ___.

A school may spend at most ₹60 on a bat costing ₹32.75 and a ball costing ₹26.40. (a) Using only the whole-number parts, between which two amounts must the total lie? (b) Can the range alone tell the school that the bill is within the limit? Decide, then find the exact total.
questions.a: (a) 32 + 26 = 58, so the total lies between 58 and 60. (b) Yes: the total is below 60, so it cannot exceed the limit of ₹60. The exact total is 32.75 + 26.40 = 59.15, which is within the limit.
s: Part (b): decides the bill is within ₹60 because the total is below 60, and finds 59.15

questions.q: (a) Find 4.1 + 3.1 and 4.9 + 3.9. (b) The whole parts 4 and 3 give the range 7 to 9. If both decimals have non-zero fractional parts, can their sum be exactly 9? Can it be exactly 7? Explain.
questions.a: (a) 4.1 + 3.1 = 7.2 and 4.9 + 3.9 = 8.8. (b) Neither. It can never be 9: that needs the two fractional parts to total 2, but each is below 1. It cannot be 7 either: two non-zero fractional parts add to more than 0, so the sum is more than 7. It lies strictly between 7 and 9.
s: Part (b): says neither, 9 impossible since fractional parts total less than 2, and 7 impossible since they total more than 0

questions.q: Rishi says: '9.1 - 4.9 lies between 4 and 6.' Is he right? Use the whole-number parts, and say why the range runs from 4 and not from 5.
questions.a: Yes. The whole parts give 9 - 4 = 5, and the difference of two decimals lies within 1 of that, so between 4 and 6. Exact: 9.1 - 4.9 = 4.2, which is inside the range. It is below 5 because 9.1 has only 0.1 above 9 while 4.9 has 0.9 above 4, so the fractional parts reduce the difference; the range must allow for that.
s: Gives the verdict that Rishi is right
Checks the exact value 4.2 and explains why it falls below 5

questions.q: Two decimals both have the whole part 12. (a) Between which two numbers must their sum lie? (b) Their sum is exactly 25.4 and each has one digit after the point. Give one possible pair and show that the sum fits your range.
questions.a: (a) 12 + 12 = 24, so the sum lies between 24 and 26. (b) The tenths must total 14 tenths (1.4 in all), for example 12.7 + 12.7 = 25.4 or 12.9 + 12.5 = 25.4. 25.4 lies between 24 and 26. Any pair whose tenths add to 14 is correct.
s: Part (b): a valid pair with tenths adding to 14 and the range check

questions.q: Write two decimals whose whole parts are 8 and 9 and whose sum is above 18.5. Show with the estimation rule that the sum cannot reach 19, and find the actual sum.
questions.a: For example 8.95 + 9.95 = 18.90. The whole parts add to 17, so the sum lies between 17 and 19, and 18.9 is above 18.5 but below 19. Any valid pair works if the sum is above 18.5.
s: Gives two valid decimals with whole parts 8 and 9
States the range 17 to 19 from the whole parts
Shows the actual sum is above 18.5 and below 19

questions.q: A baker weighs two lots of flour in pairs. For which pair does the whole-parts rule give the range 14 kg to 16 kg for the total, and is the exact total above 15 kg?
questions.a: 7.3 kg and 7.9 kg

questions.q: Estimate first and then calculate. (a) Give the range for 46.8 + 29.35. (b) Find its exact value. (c) Give the range for 46.8 - 29.35. (d) Find its exact value. (e) Using the range in (a), which of 76.5 and 77.1 can be ruled out as the sum, and which cannot?
questions.a: (a) 46 + 29 = 75: between 75 and 77. (b) 46.80 + 29.35 = 76.15. (c) 46 - 29 = 17: between 16 and 18. (d) 46.80 - 29.35 = 17.45. (e) 77.1 is above 77, so the range rules it out. 76.5 is inside 75 to 77, so the range cannot rule it out (the exact sum 76.15 shows it is still wrong).
s: Part (e): rules out 77.1 and says 76.5 cannot be ruled out by the range

questions.q: True or False: For 31.6 + 12.45 the whole-number-parts range rules out an answer of 45.5 but cannot rule out an answer of 44.5. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: True. The whole parts give 31 + 12 = 43, so the sum lies between 43 and 45. The answer 45.5 is outside this range and is rejected; 44.5 is inside it, so the range cannot reject it (the true sum 44.05 shows it is still wrong).
s: Gives the range 43 to 45 and places 45.5 outside and 44.5 inside

questions.q: Two decimals have whole parts 40 and 17. Write the range for their difference, and give a pair of decimals whose difference is near the bottom of that range.
questions.a: 40 - 17 = 23, so the difference lies between 22 and 24. For example 40.1 - 17.9 = 22.2, which is just above 22.
s: Gives a valid pair such as 40.1 - 17.9 = 22.2

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Estimating with whole-number parts can catch a decimal-point slip in a sum.
Reason (R): A sum of two decimals can differ from the sum of their whole parts by less than 2 only, but a wrongly placed decimal point makes the answer far larger or smaller than that.
o: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
questions.a: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.q: A cashier adds ₹2,345.60 and ₹1,987.45 and has ₹4,333 in the till. Using only the whole-number parts, which statement is correct?
questions.a: The range 4,332 to 4,334 cannot decide it; the exact total ₹4,333.05 is ₹0.05 more than the till
o: The range 4,332 to 4,334 cannot decide it; the exact total ₹4,333.05 is ₹0.05 more than the till
The range starts at 4,332, so the till is certainly enough
The range ends at 4,334, so the till is certainly not enough
