questions.q: At a school fair in Guwahati the morning collection was ₹4,372.60 and the afternoon collection ₹2,985.75. The treasurer reports the total as ₹7,458.35. (a) Use the whole-number parts to give a range for the total. (b) Does the reported total lie in the range? (c) Find the exact total. (d) By how much is the treasurer's figure out, and what kind of slip does that suggest?
questions.a: (a) 4372 + 2985 = 7357, so the total is between 7357 and 7359. (b) No: 7,458.35 is above 7359. (c) 4,372.60 + 2,985.75 = ₹7,358.35. (d) 7,458.35 - 7,358.35 = ₹100.00; the figure is exactly ₹100 too high, which suggests a wrong digit in the hundreds place.
s: Part (b): says the reported total is outside the range
Part (d): says a hundreds-place digit slip is suggested

questions.q:
Consider the statements about two decimals that both have non-zero fractional parts.
Statement 1: Their sum is greater than the sum of their whole-number parts.
Statement 2: Their difference is always greater than the difference of their whole-number parts.
Statement 3: Their sum is always less than the sum of their whole-number parts plus 1.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 only

questions.q: Someone says 31.4 - 12.8 = 20.4. Show that this cannot be correct without subtracting the decimals, and then find the true difference.
questions.a: Whole parts 31 and 12 give 19, so the difference lies between 18 and 20. 20.4 is outside that range, so it cannot be right. True difference: 31.4 - 12.8 = 18.6. (The difference of the whole parts is 19; the true difference can be up to 1 less or 1 more.)
s: Finds the whole parts' difference 19 and the range 18 to 20
Says 20.4 is outside the range so it is impossible

questions.q: At a school fair in Kota, a pupil adds 12.5 kg and 8.75 kg of flour, gets the right digits 2125 but writes the total as 2.125 kg. Which statement describes the whole-number-parts range and her slip?
o: The range is 20 to 22; the point was moved one place left, so her figure is 10 times too small
The range is 20 to 22; the point was moved one place right, so her figure is 10 times too large
The range is 21 to 23; the point was moved one place left, so her figure is 10 times too small
The range is 20 to 22; the point was moved two places left, so her figure is 100 times too small
questions.a: The range is 20 to 22; the point was moved one place left, so her figure is 10 times too small

questions.q: Write two decimals with whole parts 9 and 6 whose sum is exactly 16. Show that your pair fits the whole-number-parts range, and give a second pair, each number with two digits after the point, that also totals 16.
questions.a: The range is 9 + 6 = 15 to 17, and 16 sits inside it. For example 9.6 + 6.4 = 16.0. A second pair: 9.35 + 6.65 = 16.00 (the hundredths 5 + 5 = 10 and tenths 3 + 6 + 1 = 10 carry to give 6 + 9 + 1 = 16).
s: Gives a valid pair (e.g. 9.6 and 6.4) and shows 16 lies in 15 to 17
Gives a valid two-decimal-place pair totalling 16 (e.g. 9.35 and 6.65)

questions.q: Priya adds 6.9 and 5.9, which are each very close to the next whole number, and expects the sum to lie between 11 and 13. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: The rule holds, as each decimal part is still below 1
o: The rule holds, as each decimal part is still below 1
The rule fails: 6.9 is nearly 7, so the range should start at 13
The rule fails: 12.8 is too close to 13 to be inside the range
The rule holds only when both decimal parts are below one-half

questions.q:
Match each sum in Column I with the interval in Column II that, by the whole-parts rule, must contain it.
Column I: 1. 3.4 + 5.7   2. 12.5 + 0.9   3. 20.1 + 9.8   4. 7.7 + 7.7
Column II: a. 14 and 16   b. 8 and 10   c. 29 and 31   d. 12 and 14

In a charity walk at a school in Raipur, Meera walked 12.85 km on Saturday and 9.6 km on Sunday. The walk gives a badge to anyone who covers at least 22.5 km over the two days. At the finish line the coach has time only to look at the whole-number parts of the two distances in the log.
(a) Using only the whole-number parts, between which two numbers does her total lie?
(b) Can this range alone tell the coach whether Meera earned the badge? Explain.
(c) Find her exact total distance.
(d) Does she earn the badge, and by how much does her total differ from the target?
questions.a: (a) 12 + 9 = 21, so the total is between 21 and 23. (b) No: the target 22.5 lies inside the range 21 to 23, so the total could be on either side of it. (c) 12.85 + 9.60 = 22.45 km. (d) No. 22.5 - 22.45 = 0.05 km; she is 0.05 km (50 metres) short.
s: Part (b): says the target 22.5 lies inside the range so it cannot decide
Part (d): no badge, short by 0.05 km

questions.q:
A family travelling by train from Pune to Chennai packs two bags weighing 18.75 kg and 21.6 kg. The free baggage allowance is 40 kg. Excess baggage is charged ₹300 whatever the extra weight. To avoid the charge they could leave behind either a 0.3 kg storybook (free to leave) or a 0.5 kg jar of home-made pickle that would cost ₹450 to buy again at the destination.
(a) Using whole-number parts, give the range for the total weight and say whether it decides if they are within 40 kg.
(b) Find the exact total weight.
(c) Which option should the family choose: pay ₹300, leave the book, or leave the pickle? Justify with the new total weight for each option.
questions.a: (a) 18 + 21 = 39, so the total is between 39 and 41. The range cannot decide because 40 lies inside it. (b) 18.75 + 21.60 = 40.35 kg, which is 0.35 kg over. (c) Leaving the book gives 40.05 kg, still over 40, so it does not avoid the charge. Leaving the pickle gives 39.85 kg, which is within 40 but costs ₹450 to replace. Paying ₹300 is cheaper than losing the pickle, so the family should pay the ₹300 (unless they value the pickle less than ₹300).
s: Part (a): range 39 to 41 and says it cannot decide since 40 lies inside
Part (c): new totals 40.05 and 39.85, then compares ₹300 with ₹450 and decides

questions.q: In a 20-over school match in Visakhapatnam the scoreboard reads 'Overs bowled: 14.3'. (a) How many balls have been bowled? (b) How many balls are left in the innings? (c) Write the overs left as the scoreboard shows them. (d) After 2 more overs and 4 more balls, what will the scoreboard read for overs bowled?
questions.a: (a) 14 x 6 + 3 = 87 balls. (b) 120 - 87 = 33 balls. (c) 33 = 5 x 6 + 3, so 5.3 overs left. (d) 2.4 overs is 16 balls; 87 + 16 = 103 balls = 17.1. The board reads 17.1.
s: Part (d): adds 16 balls to get 103 balls

questions.q: Ritu measures a window opening as 3 ft 4 in wide but tells the carpenter 'make the window 3.4 ft wide'. (a) What width in inches does 0.4 ft stand for? (Cut 12 in into 10 equal parts first.) (b) Is the window the carpenter builds wider or narrower than the opening, by how many inches, and will it fit? (1 ft = 12 in.)
questions.a: (a) 12 in cut into 10 equal parts gives 1.2 in each tenth; 4 tenths = 1.2 + 1.2 + 1.2 + 1.2 = 4.8 in. (b) The window is 3 ft 4.8 in, wider than the opening (3 ft 4 in) by 4.8 - 4 = 0.8 in, so it will not fit.

questions.q: True or False: Two bowlers have bowled 4.3 overs and 3.4 overs. Together they have bowled 7.7 overs. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: False. The digit after the point counts balls out of 6, so 4.3 is 27 balls and 3.4 is 22 balls. Together 27 + 22 = 49 balls = 8 overs and 1 ball, which the board shows as 8.1. A score of 7.7 is impossible because an over has only 6 balls.
s: Converts to 27 + 22 = 49 balls and writes 8.1 (7.7 cannot occur on an overs board)

questions.q: Zoya says: '2.5 hours means 2 hours 50 minutes, because 0.5 is 50 hundredths.' Is she right? Explain what 2.5 hours really is.
questions.a: No. An hour has 60 minutes and is split into 10 parts of 6 minutes each. 0.5 hour is 5 such parts, 5 x 6 = 30 minutes, so 2.5 hours is 2 hours 30 minutes. Hundredths do not apply because the hour is not divided by 100 minutes.
s: Gives the verdict that Zoya is wrong
Shows each tenth of an hour is 6 minutes
Gets 5 x 6 = 30 minutes, so 2 hours 30 minutes

questions.q: Bus A's booking message says the journey takes 2.5 hours; bus B's says 2 hours 40 minutes. (a) Write 2.5 hours in hours and minutes. (b) Which bus is quicker, and by how many minutes?
questions.a: (a) 0.5 hour = 5 tenths of an hour = 5 x 6 = 30 minutes, so 2 h 30 min. (b) Bus A takes 150 minutes and bus B 160 minutes, so bus A is quicker by 10 minutes.
s: Part (a): 5 x 6 = 30 minutes, so 2 h 30 min
Part (b): compares 150 with 160 minutes: bus A quicker by 10 minutes

questions.q:
Consider the statements about decimal-looking numbers.
Statement 1: 'Overs left: 5.5' means 5 and 5/10 overs.
Statement 2: 3.4 overs bowled means 3 overs and 4 balls.
Statement 3: In '4.5 hours after noon' the 0.5 stands for 30 minutes.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 and 3 only

questions.q: A school notice starting at 9:00 a.m. lists three back-to-back items with no gaps: practice 1.5 hours, break 0.4 hour and quiz 0.7 hour. (a) Write each item's length in minutes. (b) Add the three lengths and write the total in hours and minutes. (c) At what time does the quiz end? (d) A pupil reads 1.5 hours as 1 hour 50 minutes. When would he think the practice ends, and how many minutes after the true end is that?
questions.a: (a) 1.5 h = 90 min; 0.4 h = 4 x 6 = 24 min; 0.7 h = 7 x 6 = 42 min. (b) 90 + 24 + 42 = 156 min = 2 h 36 min. (c) 9:00 + 2 h 36 min = 11:36 a.m. (d) The true end of practice is 10:30; he would think 10:50, which is 20 minutes after the true end.
s: Part (d): true end 10:30, his 10:50, 20 minutes later

questions.q: A lesson lasts 1 hour 12 minutes. A pupil writes this as 1.12 hours. (a) Say why this is wrong, using the fact that one tenth of an hour is 6 minutes. (b) Write the duration correctly in hours as a decimal.
questions.a: (a) 1.12 would mean 1 hour and 12 hundredths of an hour, but an hour is not split into 100 equal parts of minutes; one tenth of an hour is 6 minutes. (b) 12 minutes = 2 tenths of an hour (2 x 6 = 12), so the lesson lasts 1.2 hours.
s: Part (a): says 1.12 reads as hundredths but an hour splits into tenths of 6 minutes

questions.q: The school scoreboard reads 'Overs bowled: 8.5'. Karan says that after 3 more balls it will read 8.8. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: It will read 9.2, because 5 + 3 = 8 balls is one over and 2 balls
o: It will read 9.2, because 5 + 3 = 8 balls is one over and 2 balls
It will read 8.8, because the digit after the point goes up by 3
It will read 9.3, because the first ball completes the over and 3 more balls follow
It will read 9.8, because 8.5 and 3 balls make 9.8

questions.q: A railway timetable gives four running times for a route: 1.4 hours, 1 hour 35 minutes, 1.6 hours and 1 hour 28 minutes. Which running time is the longest?
questions.a: 1.6 hours

questions.q: A video app shows 'Watched: 1.9 hours'. Sana's own log says she watched for 1 hour 54 minutes, and her friend Tara wrote that she watched for 1 hour 9 minutes as '1.9 hours'. (a) Do the app and Sana's log agree? Use 1 tenth of an hour = 6 minutes. (b) By how many minutes does the app's 1.9 hours differ from Tara's real 1 hour 9 minutes?
questions.a: (a) Yes. 1.9 hours is 1 hour and 9 tenths of an hour; 9 x 6 = 54 minutes, so 1 h 54 min. (b) 1.9 hours is 114 minutes and Tara watched 69 minutes, so the difference is 114 - 69 = 45 minutes.
s: Part (a): 9 x 6 = 54 minutes, so they agree

questions.q: A coach starts a fitness drill at 4:10 p.m. The drill has two back-to-back parts: 1.3 hours of running and then 0.8 hour of stretching. At what time does the drill end?

After 94 balls of a 20-over match, a pupil writes 'Overs bowled: 9.4' by cutting 94 into 9 and 4. (a) Show that 9.4 cannot be right. (b) Write the correct scoreboard entry. (c) Write the overs left as the scoreboard would show them.
questions.a: (a) 9.4 would mean 9 x 6 + 4 = 58 balls, not 94. (b) 94 = 15 x 6 + 4, so the board reads 15.4. (c) 120 - 94 = 26 balls = 4 x 6 + 2, so 4.2 overs are left.

questions.q: Two school matches show 'Overs bowled: 12.5' and 'Overs bowled: 14.1'. Meena subtracts 14.1 - 12.5 = 1.6 and says 16 balls more have been bowled in the second match. How many balls more have actually been bowled?
questions.a: 8 balls

questions.q: Make up a short real-life message or notice that uses a decimal-looking time or an overs score. Say how a careless reader could misread it and what it really means.
questions.a: Any valid example, e.g. 'The match resumes after 1.5 hours': a careless reader may think 1 h 50 min or 1 h 5 min, but 0.5 hour is 30 minutes so it means 1 h 30 min. Or '10.3 overs' read as 10 and 3/10 instead of 10 overs and 3 balls.
s: A realistic message using a time or an overs score
Gives the correct meaning with the 60-minute or 6-ball reasoning

questions.q:
Assertion (A): In 'Overs left: 5.5' the digit 5 after the point stands for 5 balls.
Reason (R): One over has 6 balls, so the digit after the point in an overs score can be as large as 6.
questions.a: A is true but R is false.
o: A is true but R is false.
A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: A booking message says a bus leaving at 6:00 a.m. takes 3.8 hours. It arrives at ___ a.m. (write the time as hours:minutes).
Show that a scoreboard cannot correctly read 'Overs bowled: 7.8'. What would it show after 7 overs and 8 balls?
questions.a: An over has 6 balls, so the digit after the point can only be 0 to 5. 8 balls would complete one over (6 balls) and leave 2, so the bowling is 8 overs and 2 balls. The board would show 8.2.
s: States an over has 6 balls so the digit after the point is at most 5
Breaks 8 balls into one over and 2 balls

questions.q: In a 20-over match the scoreboard shows 'Overs bowled: 19.2'. Ritu subtracts 20 - 19.2 = 0.8 and says 8 balls remain. After 3 more balls are bowled, what will the scoreboard read and how many balls really remain?
questions.a: 19.5, and 1 ball remains

questions.q:
Karan must catch a train at 11:55 a.m. from a station in Bengaluru. A bus leaves the bus stand at 9:20 a.m. and the booking message says the journey takes 2.4 hours. After the bus reaches the station area, he needs 10 minutes to walk to the train platform.
(a) Write 2.4 hours in hours and minutes.
(b) At what time does the bus reach the station area?
(c) At what time would he reach the platform?
(d) Should Karan take this bus? Explain, and say how Karan's plan changes if the message had meant 2 hours 40 minutes instead.
questions.a: (a) 0.4 hour is 4 tenths of an hour, each tenth being 6 minutes, so 4 x 6 = 24 minutes and the time is 2 h 24 min. (b) 9:20 + 2 h 24 min = 11:44 a.m. (c) 11:44 + 10 min = 11:54 a.m. (d) He reaches the platform at 11:54, a minute before 11:55, so the plan works but is very tight. If the message meant 2 h 40 min the bus would arrive at 12:00 and he would miss the train, so he should be sure that 2.4 hours means 2 h 24 min; given that, the bus works but with only 1 minute to spare.
s: Part (d): says the plan works with 1 minute to spare and compares with the 2 h 40 min reading (12:00)

questions.q:
In a 20-over school final in Jaipur the scoreboard shows 'Overs bowled: 16.4'. A bowler may bowl at most 4 overs in the match. So far the fast bowler Kabir has bowled 3 overs and the spinner has bowled 3 overs. A third bowler is finishing the current over; he has bowled 2 overs so far, including this one. Every other bowler has already used up his 4 overs, so only Kabir, the spinner and the third bowler can bowl the rest. The captain now plans the 18th, 19th and 20th overs.
(a) How many balls have been bowled so far, and how many remain?
(b) How many balls are left in the current over, and how many full overs come after it?
(c) How many more overs can Kabir and the spinner bowl together, and how many of the last three overs must someone else bowl?
(d) No bowler may bowl two overs in a row, Kabir will bowl only the last over, and the spinner cannot bowl the 20th. Which over does the third bowler, who is finishing the 17th, take? Give the reason.
questions.a: (a) 16 x 6 + 4 = 100 balls bowled; 120 - 100 = 20 balls remain. (b) The 17th over has 4 of its 6 balls bowled, so 2 balls are left; the other 18 balls are 3 full overs (18th, 19th, 20th). (c) Each has 4 - 3 = 1 over left, so together they can bowl 2 overs; the third of the last three overs must be bowled by someone else (the third bowler, the only other bowler left, who has 4 - 2 = 2 overs available). (d) The third bowler bowls the 17th, so he cannot bowl the 18th. Kabir bowls only the 20th, and the spinner cannot bowl the 20th, so the 18th goes to the spinner (Kabir is saved for the 20th and the third bowler cannot follow his own over). That leaves the 19th for the third bowler, giving spinner, third bowler, Kabir with nobody bowling twice in a row. Only the 19th works.
s: Part (b): 2 balls left in the over and 3 full overs after it
Part (c): 2 overs between Kabir and the spinner, one over for someone else (the third bowler)
Part (d): rules out the 18th for the third bowler, puts Kabir on the 20th, so the spinner takes the 18th, and concludes the third bowler takes the 19th

questions.q: Fatima needs a ribbon as close to 1 m as possible, but it must not be shorter than 1 m. The pieces in the shop measure 0.8 m, 0.69 m, 1.08 m and 0.95 m. Which should she buy?
A tank shows 8.4 L, 7.9 L and 7.4 L at its first three hourly checks, and the same change continues. It must be topped up at the first check that shows less than 5 L. That is check number ___.
A sequence has a constant change. Its 2nd term is 6.35 and its 5th term is 7.55. (a) Find the change from one term to the next. (b) Find the 8th term.
questions.a: (a) From the 2nd to the 5th term there are 3 steps and the total rise is 7.55 - 6.35 = 1.20, i.e. 12 tenths shared over 3 equal steps, so each step is 4 tenths = 0.4. (b) The 6th, 7th and 8th terms are 7.95, 8.35 and 8.75, so the 8th term is 8.75.
s: Part (a): 1.20 over 3 steps gives a change of 0.4

questions.q: Four readings from a lab are 4.8, 4.75, 4.782 and 5.1. (a) Which two readings are closest to each other? (b) What is the gap between them in thousandths?
s: Part (a): picks 4.8 and 4.782 by comparing the gaps

questions.q: A water tank in a hostel shows 9.60 L, 9.15 L and 8.70 L at its first three hourly checks, and the same fall continues every hour. The school must refill the tank at the first check that reads below 7 L. Which check is that?
questions.a: The 7th check, reading 6.90 L

questions.q: Write a sequence of five decimals that starts at 2.4 and has a constant change of 0.35. Then make up a real-life situation in which such a sequence could occur.
questions.a: 2.40, 2.75, 3.10, 3.45, 3.80. Situation example: a plant grows 0.35 cm every day from a height of 2.4 cm.
s: Writes the five terms starting 2.4 with the correct change
A realistic situation with a constant change of 0.35

questions.q: Anika says: 'Among 3.2, 3.099 and 2.95, the number closest to 3 is 2.95, even though it is smaller than 3.' Is she right? Support your answer with the differences.
questions.a: Yes. The differences from 3 are 0.2 (3.2), 0.099 (3.099) and 0.05 (2.95). 0.05 = 50 thousandths is the smallest, so 2.95 is closest. Being below the target does not matter; only the size of the difference does.
s: Gives the verdict that Anika is right
Concludes the smallest difference decides, whether above or below 3

questions.q: True or False: 7.015 is closer to 7 than 6.98 is, even though 7.015 is the larger number. Give the reason or the correction.
questions.a: True. Closeness is the size of the difference from 7, not which number is bigger: 7.015 - 7 = 0.015 (15 thousandths) while 7 - 6.98 = 0.02 (20 thousandths). The smaller difference belongs to 7.015.
s: Computes the two differences 0.015 and 0.02 and picks the smaller

questions.q: Show that 7.5, 8.3 and 9.2 cannot be consecutive terms of a sequence with a constant change.
questions.a: The change from 7.5 to 8.3 is 0.8 but from 8.3 to 9.2 it is 0.9. A constant change would give the same difference both times, and 0.8 is not 0.9.
s: Concludes the changes differ so no constant change is possible

questions.q: A plant's height in cm each week is 1.2, 1.55, 1.9, ... and the same change continues. Which term of the sequence is closest to 3 cm?
questions.a: 2.95, the 6th term

questions.q: (a) How far is 4.93 from 5, in hundredths? (b) Write the number above 5 that is just as far from 5 as 4.93 is, and say which of 4.93 and 5.06 is closer to 5.
questions.a: (a) 5.00 - 4.93 = 0.07, i.e. 7 hundredths. (b) The number above 5 that is as far is 5.07. 5.06 is 6 hundredths from 5, so 5.06 is closer than 4.93 (7 hundredths).
s: Part (b): 5.07, and 5.06 is closer (6 against 7 hundredths)

questions.q: Use the digits 2, 7, 0, 5 and 9 exactly once each, with one decimal point and with no zero at the start of a whole part. (a) Make the decimal closest to 60. (b) Make the smallest decimal between 100 and 1000. (c) How far is your answer in (a) from 60?
questions.a: (a) 59.720, using 5, 9 in the whole part and 7, 2, 0 after the point. (b) 205.79: the smallest possible hundreds digit is 2, then 0, then 5, with 7 and 9 after the point. (c) 60 - 59.72 = 0.28, i.e. 28 hundredths.
s: Part (b): 205.79 with the reason for the smallest digits in the highest places

questions.q: There are nine decimals with two digits after the point strictly between 3.4 and 3.5. (a) How many of them are closer to 3.5 than to 3.4? (b) Is any of the nine exactly as far from 3.5 as from 3.4? Name it.
questions.a: (a) A decimal is closer to 3.5 when its distance from 3.5 is smaller. 3.46, 3.47, 3.48 and 3.49 are 4, 3, 2 and 1 hundredths from 3.5 but 6, 7, 8 and 9 hundredths from 3.4, so 4 of them are closer to 3.5. (b) Yes, 3.45 is 5 hundredths from each end.
s: Part (a): 3.46 to 3.49, that is 4 decimals, by comparing the two distances

Reason (R): The constant change in this sequence is +0.3, because consecutive terms differ by 0.3.
o: A and R are both true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A and R are both true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.q: Look at the sequence 2, 2.5, 2.25, 2.75, 2.5, 3, ... (a) Describe the two changes that alternate. (b) Write the next four terms. (c) Find the 10th term. (d) What is the net change over every two steps? Use it, without listing every term, to find the 19th term and then the 20th term.
questions.a: (a) Alternately add 0.5 and subtract 0.25. (b) 2.75, 3.25, 3, 3.5. (c) The 10th term is 3.5. (d) Every two steps change the value by 0.5 - 0.25 = 0.25. The 19th term is 9 pairs of steps after the first term: 2 + 9 x 0.25 = 4.25 (adding 0.25 nine times). The 20th term adds 0.5 to that: 4.75.
s: Part (d): net 0.25 per two steps; 19th term 4.25 and 20th term 4.75

questions.q:
Consider the statements.
Statement 1: To find the change in a decimal sequence we subtract each term from the next term.
Statement 2: A decimal that is below the target can never be the closest one to it.
Statement 3: In 13.5, 16, 18.5 the change is 2.5.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only

questions.q: Using the digits 1, 5, 7 and 9 exactly once each and one decimal point, make the decimal closest to 20. Give its difference from 20.
questions.a: 19.75 is the closest: 20 - 19.75 = 0.25. Others like 19.57 (0.43) and 17.95 (2.05) are further away.

questions.q: A machine should cut rods 2.5 m long, and a rod is accepted if it is within 0.05 m of 2.5 m (either side). Four rods measure 2.46 m, 2.53 m, 2.57 m and 2.43 m. How many are accepted?

Plant A in a school garden is 4.6 cm tall in week 1 and 5.2 cm tall in week 3, growing by the same amount each week. Plant B is 5.0 cm in week 1 and grows 0.2 cm each week. In which week are the two plants first equally tall, and how tall?
questions.a: Week 5, at 5.8 cm

questions.q:
A packing unit in Rajkot fills sugar bags labelled 1 kg. An inspector weighs five bags: 0.985 kg, 1.01 kg, 0.9 kg, 1.1 kg and 1.004 kg. A bag passes if its weight is within 0.01 kg of 1 kg (exactly 0.01 kg away still passes). The manager says the machine always under-fills.
(a) Which bag is closest to 1 kg, and by how many thousandths?
(b) Which bags pass the rule?
(c) Do the five readings support the manager's claim? Justify, and say what the readings suggest about the machine.
questions.a: (a) 1.004 kg, 4 thousandths away (1.01 is 10 thousandths away). (b) 1.004 and 1.01 pass; 0.985 is 15 thousandths away, which is too far. (c) No. Three bags are above 1 kg (1.01, 1.1, 1.004) and two are below (0.985, 0.9), so the machine does not always under-fill. The errors of 0.1 kg in both directions (0.9 and 1.1) suggest it is inconsistent and needs a check, not just one adjustment.
s: Part (c): shows bags both above and below 1 kg so the claim fails, and suggests an inconsistent machine

questions.q:
Tanvi and her sister Isha each save part of their pocket money in rupees every month. Tanvi saves ₹25.50 in January, ₹28.25 in February and ₹31.00 in March. Isha saves ₹40.00 in January, ₹38.25 in February and ₹36.50 in March. Both keep the same constant change each month.
(a) What is Tanvi's monthly change?
(b) How much does Tanvi save in May?
(c) How much does Isha save in May?
(d) Tanvi says she is the better saver because her savings keep rising while Isha's keep falling. Over the five months January to May, who has saved more in total? Support your answer with the totals.
questions.a: (a) 28.25 - 25.50 = ₹2.75 more each month. (b) April ₹33.75, May ₹36.50. (c) Isha's amount falls by ₹1.75 each month: April ₹34.75, May ₹33.00. (d) Tanvi's five-month total is ₹155.00; Isha's is ₹182.50. Isha has saved ₹27.50 more in total, although Tanvi's monthly saving has overtaken hers by May.
s: Part (d): totals 155.00 and 182.50, so Isha saved ₹27.50 more
